newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Four Oman cargoes, three Tapis offered to Bangchak.
newsitem.headline: Four Oman cargoes, three Tapis offered to Bangchak.

text.p: Up to four cargoes of Oman and three cargoes of Tapis crudes have been offered into Thailand's Bangchak tender for November lifting, industry sources said on Thursday.
The 120,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Bangchak Petroleum Plc refinery has tendered to buy 500,000 barrels of November Gulf crude and 600,000 barrels of light sweet Far East crudes.
The tender closed on Wednesday and offers are valid until 1800 hours Bangkok time (1100 GMT) later on Thursday.
The best Oman offers were at November Dubai quotes plus 80 cents per barrel and MPM flat, the sources said.
One of the Oman offers was for late October/early November loading.
The sources said one cargo of Iranian heavy crude was offered into the tender from a Japanese trader at Far East Iranian heavy formula, plus 10 cents.
One Dubai cargo was offered at full month quotes plus 50 cents, they said.
Two cargoes of Tapis and one indication of a third Tapis cargo were offered into the tender. The most competitive Tapis offer was between $1.15 and $1.20 a barrel, sources said.
There were no other offers of Far East crudes, the sources said.
They said the low number of offers of Oman crude was because of uncertainty over the official selling prices for September.
Oman's Ministry of Petroleum and Minerals (MPM) is expected to release its retroactive September price, which acts as the benchmark for forward trading, in coming days.
That makes it difficult for traders to assess where they should pitch their offers for the Bangchak tender.

A cargo of October Oman traded at MPM minus 50 cents and November spot trade has been slow with prices ranging between Dubai plus 82 and plus 85 cents or the equivalent of August's MPM minus 14 cents.
Oman normally trades at a differential to MPM, but spot market trading has switched to Dubai-related quotes to try to avoid exposure to the MPM base price.
